::: {#exm-forest}
#### A forest of four trees

The graph $F$ of @fig-trees-or-not is a forest (@def-forest):
taking out $d$, $f$, $g$ and $h$, which have degree 1, leaves no edges, so $F$ has no cycles, by @lem-degree-one.
Its connected components (@def-connected-component) are

- the vertex $a$, with no edges;
- the vertex $b$, with no edges;
- the vertices $c$ and $d$, with the edge $\set{c, d}$;
- the vertices $e$, $f$, $g$ and $h$, with the edges $\set{e, f}$, $\set{e, g}$ and $\set{e, h}$.

Each of them is a tree (@def-tree).
The tree $T$ of @fig-trees-or-not is a forest too,
and the graph $H$ is not a forest.

:::
